crane_bridge_bottom_h_m.what: NEAR crane (the one to park over the DJ): floor to the underside of the bridge girders, at mid-span (x 0) AND under each pick (x -5.0 and +5.6); 3 readings each
crane_bridge_bottom_h_m.where: on the floor under the bridge, meter flat on the floor, beam straight up (use the meter's tilt read-out: 90 +-0.5 deg)
crane_bridge_bottom_h_m.tolerance: +-0.05 m (the cut moves 1:1 with it; margin to the 0.5 m raised-hands rule is 0.24 m at 7.95)
crane_bridge_bottom_h_m.reads_it: hall.py (KEYS_FROM_DIMS): copy the value to the top-level key of the same name
crane_bridge_bottom_h_m.method: single-view metrology (Criminisi, Reid & Zisserman 2000): camera of 20261008_170604.jpg resected in the hall frame: (-2.2, 1.76, 5.9) m, facing +z, pitch 20.3 deg, f 1500 px (EXIF 13 mm-eq on 2992 px), on 5 left-row column consoles (6.0 m grid; C1 = grid z 18, the near end of the low block wall z 18-30) + the hall-axis vanishing point (Caprile & Torre 1990); Monte Carlo 400 draws: pixels +-6 px, f +-2 %, console x -11.1 +-0.3 m; rms 5.8 px. Script + numbers: ~/Downloads/moxir/site-2026-10-08/data/. The bridge depth comes from where its -x (house-left) end meets the runway line (1-D cross-ratio along the 6 m grid, independent of the girder height); the underside height is then read from its elevation angle at that depth.
crane_bridge_bottom_h_m.by: agent photo analysis of the owner's 2026-10-08 Galaxy S24 media (session 014FYCkghfEarsbPeE6R5ki8); no tape or laser reading exists in that media
crane_bridge_bottom_h_m.note: Agrees with the ASSUMED 7.95 within the range; NOT a substitute for the laser reading (tolerance asked: +-0.05 m). The top-level key stays null on purpose: this file is tagged "measured" and hall.py would label a photo estimate as measured.
